title: Humans or LLMs as the Judge? A Study on Judgement Bias

bias_targets.methodology: Measuring evaluators' preference shift (Attack Successful Rate) when factual errors are injected into generated answers.
Measuring evaluators' preference shift (Attack Successful Rate) when gender-biased content is introduced into generated answers.
Measuring evaluators' preference shift (Attack Successful Rate) when fake references are added to answers to simulate credibility.
Measuring evaluators' preference shift (Attack Successful Rate) when visually appealing rich content and formatting (e.g., markdown, emojis) are added to answers.
Analyzing whether evaluators disproportionately favor an answer based purely on its placement (e.g., consistently choosing the first or second option).
Statistically analyzing evaluators' voting preferences based on the length difference between answers, testing if longer answers are inherently favored.
Evaluating whether LLM judges systematically favor answers that they generated themselves over answers generated by other models.
